```{r setup, include = FALSE}
  collapse = TRUE,

set.seed(20260520L)
have_bacondecomp <- requireNamespace("bacondecomp", quietly = TRUE)
have_jsonlite    <- requireNamespace("jsonlite",    quietly = TRUE)
have_targets     <- requireNamespace("targets",     quietly = TRUE)
```

## Why this package exists

`bacipair` is the audit-grade methodology stack behind the Carbon-MRV
real-data port (`RDT-20`). The translation memo (`RDT-8 §5`) imposes a
**hard kill-gate**: the synthetic-control extension must recover the
oracle ATT on simulated staggered-treatment ground truth before any real
CER ACCU HIR-register data is touched.

This vignette demonstrates the full ground-truth-recovery audit on a
small simulated panel, mirroring the published kill-gate JSON log under
`deliverables/RDT-20/logs/oracle-recovery.json`.

## 1. Simulate a staggered-treatment BACI panel

The simulator carries an explicit oracle: the panel-average ATT is
exactly `mean(ite)` over treated post-treatment observations. Every
distribution and seed is recorded.

```{r simulate}
library(bacipair)

sim <- simulate_staggered_panel(
  seed    = 20260520L,
  n_pairs = 80L
)

cat("Oracle panel-average ATT:",
    round(sim$oracle_panel_att, 3), "pp\n")
cat("Treatment-year distribution:\n")
print(table(sim$pair_table$treatment_year))
cat("Proponent cluster sizes (top 10):\n")
print(head(sort(table(sim$pair_table$proponent_id),
                decreasing = TRUE), 10L))
```

## 2. Naive paired-DiD

The matched 1:1 comparator + TWFE is the natural starting point and the
foil for the synthetic-control estimator. Because elevation /
rainfall-climatology covary with treatment timing in this DGP, the
paired-DiD coefficient carries a small but real residual bias.

```{r paired-did}
did <- baci_paired_did(sim$panel)

cat(sprintf("Paired-DiD ATT_hat = %.3f pp  (cluster-robust SE = %.3f)\n",
            did$att_hat, did$se_cluster))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI: [%.3f, %.3f]\n", did$ci_lo, did$ci_hi))
cat(sprintf("Oracle: %.3f pp  ->  bias = %+0.3f pp\n",
            sim$oracle_panel_att,
            did$att_hat - sim$oracle_panel_att))
```

## 3. Time-varying synthetic-control comparator

The donor pool is every other pair's comparison arm; per-treated-unit
weights are simplex-constrained and chosen to minimise a joint
objective over pre-treatment outcomes and standardised static
predictors (baseline cover, elevation, rainfall climatology).

```{r synth-control}
sc <- synth_control_baci(sim$panel)

cat(sprintf("SC panel ATT_hat = %.3f pp\n", sc$panel_att_hat))
cat(sprintf("SC pre-fit RMSE  = %.3f pp\n", sc$pre_fit_rmse))
cat(sprintf("SC bias vs oracle = %+0.3f pp\n",
            sc$panel_att_hat - sim$oracle_panel_att))
```

The SC estimator should net out the elevation / climatology coupling,
recovering the oracle within the kill-gate floor of 0.15 pp on the
audit-grade run (12 replicates, n_pairs = 200). On the small-n
single-replicate run shown here, expect a wider envelope.

## 4. Proponent-level cluster bootstrap

One proponent runs many adjacent projects (Macintosh et al., 2024), so
the right inferential unit is the proponent cluster. The bootstrap
resamples whole proponents with replacement and refits the chosen
estimator.

```{r bootstrap}
boot <- proponent_cluster_bootstrap(
  sim$panel,
  estimator = "paired_did",
  n_boot    = 60L,
  seed      = 20260521L
)

cat(sprintf("Bootstrap (paired-DiD): SE = %.3f pp,  95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]\n",
            boot$se, boot$ci_lo, boot$ci_hi))
```

## 5. Goodman-Bacon decomposition (diagnostic)

The TWFE coefficient is a weighted average of all 2x2 DiD comparisons
implied by the treatment-timing structure. The Goodman-Bacon (2021)
decomposition exposes those weights; large weight on `Treated vs
Untreated` and small / non-negative weight on
`Earlier vs Later Treated` is the "clean TWFE" signature.

```{r goodman-bacon}
if (have_bacondecomp) {
  gb <- goodman_bacon_decomp(sim$panel)
  print(gb$weight_summary)
  cat(sprintf("Implied TWFE estimate from 2x2 weights: %.3f pp\n",
              gb$twfe_estimate))
} else {
  message("bacondecomp not installed - skipping decomposition.")
}
```

## 6. Compare to the published kill-gate JSON log

The audit-grade kill-gate run lives at
`deliverables/RDT-20/logs/oracle-recovery.json`. The schema below is
emitted by `write_oracle_recovery_log()`, which the
`bacipair_targets_plan()` skeleton invokes as its terminal target.

```{r log}
if (have_jsonlite) {
  log_path <- file.path(tempdir(), "oracle-recovery-vignette.json")
  write_oracle_recovery_log(
    panel             = sim,
    synth_control_fit = sc,
    paired_did_fit    = did,
    cluster_boot      = boot,
    path              = log_path
  )

  log <- jsonlite::fromJSON(log_path)
  str(log[c("oracle_panel_att", "sc_panel_att_hat", "sc_minus_oracle",
            "did_att_hat", "did_minus_oracle",
            "bootstrap_se", "bootstrap_ci_lo", "bootstrap_ci_hi")])
} else {
  message("jsonlite not installed - skipping log demonstration.")
}
```

## 7. Drop-in `targets` skeleton

`bacipair_targets_plan()` returns a list of `tar_target_raw()` calls
ready to drop into a `_targets.R`:

```{r targets-plan}
if (have_targets) {
  plan <- bacipair_targets_plan(
    simulate_args = list(seed = 20260520L, n_pairs = 80L),
    boot_args     = list(n_boot = 60L, seed = 20260521L)
  )
  print(names(plan))
} else {
  message("targets not installed - skipping plan demonstration.")
}
```
